blogPosts.title: Architecting Modern Web Apps for AI Search Engines & LLM Crawlers
blogPosts.author: Mahad Abbas
blogPosts.excerpt: Why traditional client-side SPAs fail against non-JS AI search engines (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Perplexity), and how static pre-rendering bridges the semantic discovery gap.
blogPosts.content:
In modern web development, visibility is no longer just about Googlebot. Emerging search interfaces—Perplexity, ChatGPT Search, Claude Artifacts, and Apple Intelligence—crawl and index websites using strict headless or static parsers that often ignore client-side JavaScript execution. ### The Problem with Pure Client-Side Rendering When a crawler requests your SPA, it often receives an empty `
` shell. While Googlebot eventually queues a Chromium renderer, LLM scrapers prioritize speed and often drop pages that don't serve meaningful HTML within 300ms. ### The Hybrid Solution 1. Static Pre-Rendering (SSG) for all public discovery routes (Home, Services, Case Studies, Blogs). 2. Structured JSON-LD schema with rich entity graphs. 3. Micro-caching via Cloudflare / Edge CDNs to deliver raw HTML in under 50ms. By adopting these architectural patterns at DigiHust, our client platforms achieve instant indexing across both traditional and AI-driven search engines.

blogPosts.title: Automating Business Workflows: n8n vs. Custom Python LLM Microservices
blogPosts.author: Abdul Raffy
blogPosts.excerpt: A practical engineering comparison for enterprise teams choosing between visual automation canvas tools and tailored Python microservices.
blogPosts.content:
Enterprise automation usually starts with a simple question: should we build on a visual workflow engine like n8n or develop custom Python microservices?

### When to Choose n8n
- Quick API orchestration (CRM to Slack, Email triggers to Webhooks).
- Non-technical stakeholder visibility into the pipeline.
- Self-hosted compliance without paying high SaaS fees.

### When to Build Custom Python Microservices
- Complex LLM agents with multi-turn memory and tool-calling validation.
- Strict latency requirements (<100ms response times).
- High-throughput asynchronous batch processing.

At DigiHust, our AI Squad uses a hybrid architecture: n8n for rapid integration plumbing, backed by containerized FastAPI endpoints for proprietary algorithms.

blogPosts.title: The Essential OWASP Web Application Security & Hardening Checklist
blogPosts.author: Muhammad Haris Asad Khan
blogPosts.excerpt: Actionable security measures to protect modern SaaS applications from injection attacks, broken access controls, and cloud privilege escalation.
blogPosts.content:
Security is not an afterthought; it is an architectural foundation. Here are the core controls we enforce across every production DigiHust application:

1. **Row Level Security (RLS)**: Never rely solely on client-side role filtering. Every table in your database must have explicit PostgreSQL policies.
2. **Cryptographic Salt Hashing**: Passwords and session secrets must use salted SHA-256 or Argon2.
3. **Content Security Policy (CSP)**: Disallow untrusted inline scripts and lock down frame ancestors to prevent clickjacking.
4. **Audit Telemetry**: Every privilege escalation, role modification, and sensitive data access must generate an immutable audit log.

Implementing these 4 pillars prevents 95% of common web vulnerabilities before your product touches production.
